title: Parameter and Argument
definition: A parameter names an input position in a function definition, while an argument is the value-producing expression supplied to that position during a call.
purpose: Make incoming data flow and caller-to-callee responsibilities explicit.
history: Parameter-passing mechanisms are foundational to procedural abstraction and differ across languages; ECMAScript binds evaluated argument values to formal parameters.
mental_model: Parameters are labeled seats in the function; arguments are the values placed into those seats for one call.
analogy: Labeled seats; it fails if it suggests objects themselves are copied deeply or that positions alone express semantic units.
common_mistakes: Using parameter and argument interchangeably without context
Relying on missing arguments becoming undefined
Mutating an object through a parameter without contract
industry_notes: Small explicit input surfaces reduce coupling; related values may need a meaningful model rather than an ever-growing positional list.
ai_notes: Require AI to justify every parameter and identify unused, derived, duplicated, or hidden input.
interview_notes: Ask how JavaScript value passing explains primitive reassignment versus object-property mutation.
